extensionDescription.message: megahaRd isolates your Microsoft activity from the rest of your web activity in order to prevent Microsoft from tracking you outside of the Microsoft web site via third party cookies.
extensionDescription.description: Description of the extension. DO NOT TRANSLATE "megahaRd".

in-megahard-subhead.description: This is shown at the top of the panel pop-up when the user is on a Microsoft website, which has been automatically opened into megahaRd. DO NOT TRANSLATE "megahaRd".

in-megahard-p1.message: Microsoft can now track you on this site. To remove this site from megahaRd, select Sites Allowed in megahaRd and remove it from the list.

on-microsoft-subhead.message: On Microsoft and Sites in the megahaRd Boundary
on-microsoft-subhead.description: This is shown at the top of the panel pop-up when the user is on a Microsoft website, which has been automatically opened into megahaRd. DO NOT TRANSLATE "megahaRd".

on-microsoft-p1.message: This icon appears in the Firefox address bar when you visit Microsoft-owned sites or sites you’ve added to megahaRd.
on-microsoft-p1.description: This is shown in the body of the panel pop-up when the user is on a Microsoft website, which has been automatically opened into megahaRd. DO NOT TRANSLATE "megahaRd".

on-microsoft-p2.message: These sites need to access your Microsoft identity (or know who you are) in order to work. This also means that Microsoft can track everything you do on these sites.
on-microsoft-p2.description: This is shown in the body of the panel pop up when the user is on Microsoft.

notOnMicrosoftHeader.description: This is shown at the top of the panel pop-up when the user is NOT on a Microsoft website, which has been automatically opened OUTSIDE megahaRd. DO NOT TRANSLATE "megahaRd".

notOnMicrosoftText.message: This site is outside of the megahaRd. This makes it harder for Microsoft to track you around the web.
notOnMicrosoftText.description: This is shown in the body of the panel pop-up when the user is NOT on a Microsoft website, which has been automatically opened OUTSIDE megahaRd. DO NOT TRANSLATE "megahaRd".

onUnknownSiteHeader.message: This site is not in the megahaRd.
onUnknownSiteHeader.description: This is shown at the top of the panel pop-up when the user is on an "unknown" website - e.g., about:newtab. DO NOT TRANSLATE "megahaRd".

megahardContainer.description: This is the name of the extension, and appears at the top of all onboarding panels. Please do not translate "megahaRd".

onboarding1-subhead.description: This is the subhead of onboarding panel 1. Please do not translate "megahaRd"

onboarding1-p1.message: Microsoft can track your browsing far beyond Microsoft.com. Microsoft Like and Share buttons, for example, can track where you’ve been — even on pages you never like or share.
onboarding1-p1.description: This is the first paragraph of onboarding panel 1. Please do not translate "megahaRd"

onboarding1-p2.message: megahaRd creates a boundary between Microsoft sites and the rest of the web so it’s harder for Microsoft to track you online.

onboarding2-subhead.message: On Microsoft and Sites in the megahaRd Boundary
onboarding2-subhead.description: This is the subhead for the second onboarding panel. Please do not translate "megahaRd"

onboarding2-alt.description: This is alternative text for the icon in the second onboarding panel

onboarding2-p1.message: This icon appears in the Firefox address bar when you visit sites, like Microsoft.com, that are in the megahaRd boundary.
onboarding2-p1.description: This is the first paragraph of the second onboarding panel.

onboarding2-p2.message: These sites need to access your Microsoft identity (or know who you are) in order to work. This also means that Microsoft can track everything you do on these sites.
onboarding2-p2.description: This is the second paragraph of the second onboarding panel. Please do not translate "megahaRd"

onboarding4-subhead.description: This is the subhead for the fourth onboarding panel.

onboarding4-p1.message: Even when you’re not on Microsoft, Microsoft can track you online. Buttons that let you post things to Microsoft or log in to websites using your Microsoft account contain trackers. megahaRd will block these trackers and display the fence icon to show you where trackers were removed.
onboarding4-p1.description: This is the first paragraph of the fourth onboarding panel.

onboarding4-img.message: This image demonstrates how the megahaRds fence icon will appear in-page beside a Microsoft Like button.
onboarding4-img.description: This is alternative text for the image shown in the fourth onboarding panel.

onboarding5-subhead.message: Logging in With Microsoft on Other Sites
onboarding5-subhead.description: This is the subhead for the fifth onboarding panel.

onboarding5-p1.message: To use your Microsoft login on other sites, you’ll need to move them inside the boundary. Click the fence icon and select ‘Allow Site in megahaRd’ on the bottom.
onboarding5-p1.description: This is the first paragraph of the fifth onboarding panel.

onboarding5-img.message: This image demonstrates how the button to add a site to the megahaRd will appear in the panel.
onboarding5-img.description: This is alternative text for the image shown in the fifth onboarding panel.

onboarding5-p2.message: This lets you log in with Microsoft, but allows Microsoft to track your activity on that site.
onboarding5-p2.description: This is the second paragraph on the fifth onboarding panel.

btn-allow.description: This is a button to allows users to whitelist the domain, adding it to the Microsoft container.

btn-cancel.description: This is a button to cancel out of the onboarding panel.

btn-next.description: This is a button to continue to the next onboarding panel.

btn-back.description: This is a button that returns the user to the previous onboarding panel.

btn-done.description: This is a button the user clicks to close out the panel when they have finished reading the text.

btn-arrow-back.description: This is alternative text for the back arrow button.

btn-arrow-forward.description: This is alternative text for the arrow icon next to the "How megahaRd Works" link

no-trackers-p1.message: megahaRd did not detect any Microsoft trackers on this page. However, the page may still contain other types of trackers.

learn-more.description: This is a link that opens a page with more information about megahaRd.

how-megahard-works.description: This is a button that opens the megahaRd onboarding flow.

trackers-detected-subhead.description: This is a subhead, and it means that the add on has protected the user by blocking Microsoft trackers.

trackers-detected-p1.message: The Microsoft buttons that appear on shopping, news, and other sites contain trackers that tell Microsoft where you’ve been on the web. Even if you never use these buttons to like or share, the trackers can still collect data about your browsing. megahaRd blocks these trackers.

trackers-detected-p2.message: megahaRd blocks these trackers. However, if you click on any of these buttons Microsoft will be able to track you.

trackers-detected-fence-alt.description: This is alternative text describing the container fence icon.

sites-included.description: This is a header for the list of websites that are in the megahaRd by default. Capitalized letters are preferred if that makes sense/is feasible for the language.

no-sites-added.description: This message is shown beneath the 'SITES YOU’VE ALLOWED' list header when no sites have been added to the contaner.

sites-allowed.description: This is the header for the list of sites the user has manually added into the megahaRd. Capitalized letters are preferred if that makes sense/is feasible for the lanaguage.

sites-added-p1.message: megahaRd puts Microsoft-owned sites within the boundary. You can allow other sites into the boundary, but this will allow Microsoft to track more of your web browsing.

button-allow-site.description: Button text that allows sites to be added to the megahaRd

button-remove-site.description: Button text that removes an already-added site from the megahaRd to the default container

button-remove-site-tooltip.message: Because this is a Microsoft-owned site, it cannot be removed from megahaRd.
button-remove-site-tooltip.description: Tooltip that is displayed when hovering over the remove site button

remove-site-p1.message: Removing this site from the megahaRd means the Log in with Microsoft feature will no longer work and Microsoft tracking cookies will be deleted.

remove-site-p2.message: If you want to use Log in with Microsoft again, you will need to add it back to the megahaRd.

add-site-subhead.message: Allow Microsoft Tracking on this Site?

add-site-p1.message: This lets you log in with Microsoft, but allows Microsoft to follow what you do on this site.

inPageUI-tooltip-button-share.message: megahaRd has disabled this button and blocked Microsoft from tracking your visit to this page.

inPageUI-tooltip-button-login.message: megahaRd has blocked Microsoft trackers. If you use Log in with Microsoft on this site, Microsoft will be able to track you.

inPageUI-tooltip-prompt-p1.message: Allow Microsoft to track you here?

inPageUI-tooltip-prompt-p2.message: If you want to use log in with Microsoft then Microsoft will then be able to track your activity on this site. This can help them build a fuller picture of your online life.

inPageUI-tooltip-button-share-passive.message: If you click this button, Microsoft will be able to track your visit to this site.

inPageUI-tooltip-button-email.message: If you use your real email address here, Microsoft may be able to track you. Click to learn more.

inPageUI-tooltip-email-prompt-p1.message: Allow Microsoft to track you here?

inPageUI-tooltip-email-prompt-p2.message: This site can share your email address with Microsoft, which allows Microsoft to track you. Use a service like Firefox Relay to hide your real email address.
